clue.text: High court judges?

parts.note: not senior lawyers but the officials perched on tall chairs beside a tennis court, ruling on play

explanation.definitionFit: Tennis officials who sit on a raised chair at the court and rule on points are called by this title.

clue.text: Straight pizzicato?

explanation.definitionFit: Not bent describes something straight; pizzicato strings are plucked rather than played with the bow.

clue.text: Framework is safe to hold a farm animal

indicators.note: the safe word is made to hold the other pieces within it

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
a ram is a male sheep kept on a farm

explanation.surface: A strongbox has been used to secure a farm beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of limits or terms within which something operates is its framework.

clue.text: Wanton siren out of bed

indicators.note: wanton means unruly or undisciplined, so the letters of siren run wild

explanation.surface: A seductive temptress has got up for the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has got up in the morning has left their bed.

clue.text: Son flusters badly under strain

indicators.note: badly signals that the word flusters is put together wrongly, so it is rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy gets badly agitated when put under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation that puts one under strain is tense and taxing.

clue.text: No short answers to Boadicea's corsets

indicators.note: no means the named letters are to be absent from the queen's name

parts.note: Boadicea, the British warrior queen, with the S of the possessive kept
A is the abbreviation for answer, so two answers shortened give two As

explanation.surface: The ancient British queen's undergarments come without any back-chat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are close-fitting upper garments for women, laced or boned to shape the torso.

clue.text: Orwell's bachelor-pad?

definitions.note: read as Orwell is, the novelist's real surname

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in degrees
pad and lair are both slang for one's home or den

explanation.surface: The writer George Orwell had a flat of his own as a single man.
explanation.walkthrough: George Orwell was the pen name of Eric Arthur Blair; the 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: The author known as George Orwell was born with this surname, his pen name hiding it.

clue.text: No night train from Glasgow Academy, for example

parts.note: the opposite of night is day
to train is to school or teach

explanation.surface: There is no overnight rail service from a Scottish city school.
explanation.walkthrough: Glasgow Academy is an independent school whose pupils go home each evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasgow Academy is an example of a school whose pupils attend by day rather than board.

clue.text: Hamstring spasm

explanation.definitionFit: To hamstring is to restrict or hamper someone; a spasm is a painful muscle contraction.

clue.text: Distinguished chief constable?

explanation.walkthrough: A special constable is a part-time volunteer police officer in the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinguished means out of the ordinary; chief means main, and a volunteer police officer in Britain is called that kind of constable.

clue.text: Toasts a poet

explanation.definitionFit: Toasts means scorches with heat; Robert Burns is Scotland's national poet.

clue.text: Ripe variety of Edam, processed before sale

parts.note: ripe fruit is ready to eat

indicators.note: a variety of the word Edam is its letters in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A mature type of Dutch cheese, prepared before going on the market.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods already manufactured and finished before going on sale are prefabricated.

clue.text: Ladies' man would be more prudent steering clear of sultanate

indicators.note: steering clear means skirting around, so the prudent word goes round the sultanate

parts.note: more prudent means wiser
Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian Peninsula

explanation.surface: A philanderer would do well to avoid an Arab state.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladies' man is a philanderer who chases many women.

clue.text: Grainless tropic isle

indicators.note: grain here is corn, and less says it is taken away from the tropic

parts.note: the Tropic of Capricorn is the southern line of latitude

explanation.surface: A tropical island where no cereal is grown.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove CORN from CAPRICORN to leave the Italian island.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples.

clue.text: Prevent timid creatures swallowing end of root

indicators.note: the timid animals take in the next piece, so it goes inside them

parts.note: deer are shy, easily startled animals

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of root

explanation.surface: Shy animals eat the tip of a root.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter is to discourage or stop someone acting.

clue.text: Rhizome to become established on range

parts.note: to take root is to become established
a range of goods for sale is stock

explanation.surface: A plant stem settles in on open grazing land.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground stem that sends out roots and shoots is a botanical synonym.

clue.text: Mathematical product shown thus!

parts.note: the exclamation mark is itself the notation for multiplying all whole numbers down to one

explanation.definitionFit: The product of every whole number from one up to n is written n with an exclamation mark.

clue.text: Pouring bad egg into sausage skin?

indicators.note: into puts the rogue inside the skin

parts.note: a sausage is filled into a casing
a bad egg is a cad, a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A rotten egg is being squeezed into a sausage case.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling in a rush like a waterfall is to be flowing or streaming down.

clue.text: Composition not conceived in a study

explanation.definitionFit: A short piece of music is called by this name; something not prepared in advance is improvised.

clue.text: Grotesque figures cooking royal eggs

indicators.note: cooking the words royal and eggs mixes their letters up

explanation.surface: Ugly faces appear while a regal breakfast is being prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: Carved monsters on church roofs, often serving as waterspouts, are grotesque figures.

clue.text: Got filed under "G"

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece is written under the letter

parts.note: to file a surface is to rasp it

explanation.surface: Something was put in an office cabinet under the letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: To have grasped something is to have understood it, to have got it.

clue.text: Nobody's boy makes such a bloomer

explanation.walkthrough: The Diary of a Nobody is a comic Victorian novel by George and Weedon Grossmith.
explanation.definitionFit: Lupin is the son of Charles Pooter in The Diary of a Nobody; a lupin is a tall garden flower.

clue.text: Salt treatment for tertian

indicators.note: giving treatment to tertian reworks its letters

explanation.surface: A medicinal salt is given as treatment for a recurring fever.
explanation.walkthrough: Tertian is a fever recurring every other day, such as malaria.
explanation.definitionFit: A compound of nitric acid is a chemical salt.

clue.text: Mercator's work finally curtailed

indicators.note: curtailed means its last letter is cut off

parts.note: at last means finally

explanation.surface: The mapmaker's project is at last cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerardus Mercator published the first book of maps given this name.

clue.text: Turner employed it to represent foam, mainly

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: lather is soapy foam

explanation.surface: The painter Turner used it to depict sea spray.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner looks like J. M. W. Turner the painter; it is a woodturner.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodturner shapes wood on a spinning machine tool.

clue.text: A watermark, fixed of course

parts.note: a mark on the water, moored in place to show the line of a racecourse for rowers

explanation.definitionFit: An anchored boat marking the start or turning point of a rowing race fills this role.

clue.text: Society takes a measure of herring for food

parts.note: a cran is a measure of fresh herring, about 750 fish

explanation.surface: A society takes a quantity of herring for its dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: SCRAN is British slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Scran is informal British slang for grub or eats.

clue.text: Relaxes and stops head falling off

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for stops is lost

parts.note: ceases means stops

explanation.surface: Someone loosens up and prevents a head from dropping off.
explanation.definitionFit: To relax tension or pain is to lessen or loosen it.

clue.text: This old mixed stew needs an air-freshener!

explanation.definitionFit: Originally the term meant a stew of mixed meats; now it is a bowl of scented dried petals.

clue.text: Old photograph found in house piano-stool

indicators.note: found in says the letters are inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An old snapshot turns up in a piano stool at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Old photographs often have a brownish tint, after the ink of the cuttlefish.

clue.text: Soft leather serves the family

parts.note: to do for someone is to serve them, and does can mean serves, as in it does for me
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: Fine leather goods are what keep the family going.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft leather made from the skin of a female deer.

clue.text: A sign of Wren's character, assimilating an ancient city

indicators.note: assimilating means taking in, so the character absorbs the city

parts.note: Beau Geste is the hero of P. C. Wren's novel
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city

explanation.surface: An emblem of the architect Wren's personality incorporates an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: Wren looks like the architect Christopher Wren; he is the novelist P. C. Wren.
explanation.definitionFit: A gesture is a movement that signals something, a sign.
